newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse gets two new listings.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse gets two new listings.

text.p: The Bucharest stock exchange said on Monday the number of listed stocks would rise to 34 this week, when another two companies join in trading.
Steel pipe maker Ciprom SA and engineering company Sinterom SA will join the stock exchange on Tuesday, trading on the second tier, a bourse statement said.
The Bucharest stock exchange lists four companies on the first tier, all in the chemical and pharmaceuticals sectors.

Ciprom, based in Ploiesti, 60 km (37 miles) north of Bucharest, has a share capital of 40.32 billion lei, in shares with a nominal value of 1,000 lei each. Individual shareholders have a stake of 59.96 percent and Romania's State Ownership Fund (FPS) holds 40.04 percent, the statement said.
It said Ciprom's development plans included boosting productivity with the help of new equipment and management restructuring.

The other newcomer Sinterom, based in the Transylvanian city of Cluj, has a share capital of 28.22 billion lei, in shares with a face value of 25,000 lei each. The FPS has a majority 70 percent stake, a private ownership fund holds 12.43 percent and individual shareholders have 17.57 percent.

Traders expected the new listings to lend some vigour to the second tier, but said investors would continue to focus on first-tier stocks, which are more liquid and boast better financial performance.
